stem: In a cohort of 100 newborn boys, about how many would be expected to remain undescended by 3 months?
explanation: About 1 to 2 boys would remain undescended by 3 months. Although cryptorchidism is seen in 3 to 5% at birth, most testes descend spontaneously, leaving only about 1 to 2% undescended at 3 months.

citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

rationale: : Many undescended testes descend spontaneously early in infancy. The relevant persistence figure is about 1 to 2% by 3 months, which corresponds to 1 to 2 boys in a cohort of 100.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because about 1 to 2% of newborn boys remain undescended by 3 months, which equals about 1 to 2 boys out of 100.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because 5 to 10% is higher than the expected persistence rate at 3 months.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because 15 to 20% substantially overestimates the proportion remaining undescended by 3 months.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because 25 to 30% is far above the expected rate by 3 months.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because 40 to 50% would imply persistence in nearly half of newborn boys, which is not consistent with spontaneous descent.
